items.reason: The factory reuses a pool shut down by the previous strategy, causing submissions after rebalance to fail and unprocessed messages to be marked complete.
Shutdown stops workers before accepted work drains and stops the commit thread before final completed offsets can be committed.
Unbounded worker queues and unconditional submission provide no backpressure, allowing queued work to exhaust memory.
Replacement strategies receive the same permanently shut-down factory pool, allowing failed submissions to be committed without processing.

The comment identifies unconditional completion of failed processing as contradicting the successful-processing-only commit guarantee. Its suggested documentation fix does not change the shared problem.
The documented backpressure guarantee contradicts the unbounded queues and absence of capacity checks or rejection.
The worker completes offsets in finally after processing exceptions, allowing failed results to be committed and permanently skipped.
Closing a strategy destroys the factory-owned shared pool, which subsequent strategies reuse, causing unprocessed submissions to be marked complete.
The ordering test uses identical results and checks only their count, so reversed processing would pass.
The concurrency test checks only completion and group coverage, so a serial implementation would pass.
The test checks for absent commits after only 0.2 seconds, before the one-second commit loop can expose the erroneous commit.
The shutdown test only checks that the factory cleared its pool reference, which does not establish that work drained or workers stopped.
Unconditional complete_offset in finally makes failed processing committable, permanently skipping failed results.
The factory hands replacement strategies the pool destroyed by the previous strategy, allowing failed submissions to be committed without processing.
Setting the worker shutdown flag before draining causes workers to exit with accepted work still queued, defeating graceful shutdown.
